verdict: Preserve the V5 foundation, wordmark and palette. The identity is coherent, but dark-silhouette legibility and a matched V5 GitHub package need work before public adoption. Audience recognition remains untested.
evidenceInspected: assets/brand/heynag-moth-v5.png, heynag-moth-v5-refined.png and heynag-moth-v5-night.png viewed directly
assets/brand/header-light.png, header-dark.png and heynag-moth-avatar-v2.png viewed directly
strengths: The longer viewer-right paddle, cream scalloped head, dark oval eyes and pale-over-green wings form a repeatable set of visual identifiers. The refined raster retains the foundation's compact body and attached feet.

The large outlined heyNag wordmark remains clear in the fresh phone-width README proof. Quiet Schibsted Grotesk leaves expression to the character; the following first-person introduction keeps Nag present.

Paper/ink reading colors, one chartreuse accent and forest for light-ground links create useful role separation. The rig shares geometry across themes; theme changes alter paints and edge treatment instead of anatomy.

findings.finding: The profile draft loads unversioned header PNGs containing the taller V2 moth with simpler wings. Fresh desktop/phone proofs confirm readable name-first hierarchy. Neither these headers nor the V2 avatar establishes a V5 application; this is a coverage gap, not a V5 construction defect.
findings.recommendation: Before a V5 release, retain a labeled V2 draft or assemble matching reviewed V5 header/avatar exports. Preserve the successful name-first hierarchy.
findings.verification: Inspect the exact packaged header and avatar together at desktop and phone widths, with both GitHub themes and complete antenna tips.

findings.finding: The fresh sheet shows small full figures losing wing/face detail at 32–48px. The legacy avatar preserves a readable face but its circular mask cuts the longer paddle. No V5 tiny avatar is established; a full-body 96px recommendation does not solve this use.
evidence: evidence/identity.png full-body rows and legacy avatar row
findings.recommendation: Define separate full-body and avatar limits. Evaluate the existing V5 construction in its intended circle before choosing a crop; preserve complete asymmetric tips.
findings.verification: Inspect 24/32/48/64px circles and 96/128/160px full figures on paper and ink for face readability, intact tips, edge clearance and wing layering.

findings.finding: Dark antenna stems fade into the ground in both the retained V2 header and current V5 rig. In the fresh small-size night rows, green paddles can read as detached. The V5 raster retains a somewhat clearer edge, but shared geometry alone does not produce equivalent silhouette readability across themes.
evidence: brand/animation-v5/character.js NIGHT palette and edge filter
findings.recommendation: Tune night-edge separation on actual application grounds before adoption, preserving the dark outline and restrained lighting. Evaluate silhouette continuity separately from wordmark contrast.
findings.verification: At 96–160px and header phone size, stems must remain visibly connected to head and paddles, with readable wing/foot boundaries and no conspicuous halo.

findings.finding: The fresh rest comparison still reads as one character family: large cream head, four wings and asymmetric paddles survive. The SVG has a wider smile, changed mitten/ruff contours and cleaner surfaces. These are visible adaptation choices, not evidence that the entire rig needs rebuilding.
findings.recommendation: Record deliberate differences and keep reference pairs for rest, thinking and one broad expression. Match visible figure height for proportion judgments; the current sheet matches image boxes.
findings.verification: Compare head/body ratio, face landmarks, antenna reach, mitten size and wing overlap at matched visible size in both themes.

findings.finding: The checksum inventory helps, but its shared draft status does not encode permitted uses of legacy assets, candidates and the rig. Prose carries that distinction; design-system.md still says expressions and motion follow although they exist.
findings.recommendation: Maintain one application map with asset version, surface, theme pair and release state; reconcile stage language. Historical filenames should not determine asset selection.
findings.verification: A new contributor can select the correct GitHub header, avatar and motion source without reading review history or guessing from suffixes.

keep: Exact heyNag capitalization and outlined wordmark
V5's head-dominant anatomy and asymmetric paddles
challengeForOtherRoles: Brand: what evidence would justify replacing the readable wordmark? Distinctiveness currently comes from the combined system.
Visual development: distinguish identity drift from useful adaptation. Which contour differences change the perceived character, and which simply support articulation?
Interaction: treat the suggested one-third-to-one-half character share as an introduction pattern. Demonstrate findable name and real project destinations when the character dominates.
limits: No audience recognition testing or legal clearance.
Fresh README proofs render local content, not live GitHub. The identity comparison uses equal image boxes, not equal visible figure height.
Direct source, assets and fresh captures inspected before peer findings; no independent browser session.
